# Worker Agent Cloud — Full Documentation

> Worker Agent.Cloud is the autonomous operating system for AI content networks: research trends, create content, enforce governance, run channels, and learn from every result.

1. [Product Overview](#product-overview)

## Product Overview

Worker Agent.Cloud is a Mission Control interface for AI content networks. It connects research, creation, governance, economics, and autonomy into a single operating loop.

### Key Features

- **Research**: Trend forecasting, competitor analysis, market scoring across live data sources.
- **Creation**: Agent workflows, content generation, asset intelligence.
- **Governance**: Compliance, brand safety, audit trails, and human approval gates.
- **Growth**: A/B experimentation, timing optimization, channel analytics.
- **Economics**: ROI intelligence, budget allocation, revenue signal tracking.
- **Autonomy**: Provider routing, pipeline orchestration, continuous learning loops.

### Mission Control

The authenticated web application at `/dashboard` provides a conversational command surface where users interact with AI agents through natural language. Key capabilities:

- Decompose content missions from market opportunities
- Route actions through governed execution pipelines
- Interpret performance telemetry and recommend next actions
- Conduct deep web research with real-time SSE streaming

---

## Architecture

### Stack

| Layer        | Technology                          |
|-------------|--------------------------------------|
| Frontend    | React 19 + Vite + TypeScript        |
| Styling     | Tailwind CSS (custom dark theme)    |
| State       | React Query                         |
| API Client  | tRPC (type-safe RPC)                |
| Backend     | Bun / Elysia / tRPC                 |
| Database    | PostgreSQL (primary)                |
| Cache       | Redis (rate-limiting, queues)       |
| Real-time   | Server-Sent Events (SSE)            |
| Hosting     | Vercel (frontend), Docker/Bun (API) |

### Project Structure

```
.
├── client/                  # React frontend (Vite + TypeScript)
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── marketing/       # LandingPage, public marketing pages
│   │   ├── mission-control/ # CommandCenter, authenticated app
│   │   ├── features/         # Feature modules (agents, pipelines, etc.)
│   │   ├── lib/              # tRPC client, utils
│   │   ├── hooks/            # Custom React hooks
│   │   └── App.tsx
│   └── index.html           # PWA shell with OG tags + schema.org
├── server/                  # Backend API (tRPC routers)
│   ├── routers/             # 18 tRPC routers
│   │   ├── _app.ts          # Router registry
│   │   ├── auth.ts
│   │   ├── script.ts
│   │   ├── ledger.ts
│   │   ├── godMachine.ts
│   │   ├── campaign.ts
│   │   ├── ide.ts
│   │   ├── connectors.ts
│   │   ├── settings.ts
│   │   ├── pipeline.ts
│   │   ├── workflow.ts
│   │   ├── knowledge.ts
│   │   ├── agents.ts
│   │   ├── tools.ts
│   │   ├── governance.ts
│   │   ├── artifacts.ts
│   │   ├── ops.ts
│   │   ├── youtubeStudio.ts
│   │   └── chat.ts
│   └── _core/               # Core infrastructure
├── deployment/              # Production deployment artifacts
│   ├── rc1/                 # Release candidate 1
│   │   ├── 001_worker_agent_baseline.sql
│   │   ├── verify-schema.sql
│   │   └── env.template
│   ├── nginx/

│   ├── systemd/
│   │   ├── worker-agent-api.service
│   │   └── worker-agent-worker.service
│   └── scripts/
│       └── bootstrap.sh
├── drizzle/sql/             # Drizzle ORM migrations
└── package.json             # Root workspace
```

### Data Flow

1. User sends a message in Mission Control
2. Request flows through tRPC router to backend agent
3. Agent may stream SSE events back in real-time
4. Results are stored in PostgreSQL
5. Learning loop extracts patterns into Knowledge Base
6. Patterns inform future agent decisions

---

## Core Concepts

### Organizations

All resources are scoped to an organization. Users belong to organizations with roles (owner, admin, editor, commenter, viewer).

### Agents

Autonomous AI workers with configurable models, providers, and instructions. Agents can be assigned to pipeline steps and execute tasks.

### Pipelines

Multi-step execution workflows composed of ordered steps (research, create, review, publish, monitor). Each step can be assigned an agent and has its own configuration.

### Campaigns

Time-bound content initiatives with budgets, start/end dates, and status tracking.

### Connectors

Platform integrations (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, etc.) for content creation and analytics.

### Knowledge Base

Vector-backed storage for learned patterns, competitor intelligence, and market data. Supports semantic search via pgvector.

---

## API Reference

### Authentication

All API endpoints require authentication via HTTP-only session cookies. OAuth is supported through GitHub, Google, and Microsoft.

### tRPC Routers

| Router         | Purpose                              |
|---------------|--------------------------------------|
| auth          | Login, logout, session management   |
| script        | Script generation and management    |
| ledger        | Billing, subscriptions, costs     |
| godMachine    | High-level orchestration engine     |
| campaign      | Campaign CRUD + lifecycle         |
| ide           | Idea generation and enrichment      |
| connectors    | Platform integrations             |
| settings      | Application settings              |
| pipeline      | Pipeline and step management      |
| workflow      | Workflow definitions and runs     |
| knowledge     | Knowledge base + vector search    |
| agents        | Agent configuration and runs      |
| tools         | Tool integrations               |
| governance    | Compliance and approval gates   |
| artifacts     | Content assets and media        |
| ops           | Operational metrics and health  |
| youtubeStudio | YouTube Studio analytics        |
| chat          | Conversational AI + SSE stream  |

### SSE Endpoints

- `GET /sse/research` — Real-time research progress events
- `GET /sse/agents` — Agent status updates
- `GET /sse/pipelines` — Pipeline execution events

---

## Agents

Agents are autonomous AI workers configured with:

- A **model** (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, Gemini 2.5, etc.)
- A **provider** (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter, etc.)
- **Instructions** (system prompt)
- **Config** (temperature, max tokens, tools, etc.)

### Agent Lifecycle

```
idle → running → completed   (normal)
idle → running → error       (failure)
idle → paused                (manual)
```

### Available Agents

1. **Research Agent** — Trend analysis, competitor intelligence
2. **Creation Agent** — Content generation, script writing
3. **Governance Agent** — Compliance checking, brand safety
4. **Optimization Agent** — Performance analysis, A/B testing

---

## Pipelines

Pipelines are ordered workflows that automate content production:

1. **Research** — Analyze market opportunities
2. **Select** — Choose the best opportunity
3. **Create** — Generate content assets
4. **Govern** — Run compliance checks
5. **Approve** — Human review (optional)
6. **Publish** — Distribute to connected platforms
7. **Measure** — Collect performance metrics
8. **Learn** — Extract patterns for next cycle

### Pipeline Statuses

- draft → running → completed (success)
- draft → running → failed (error)
- Any → paused (manual)
- Any → cancelled (manual)

---

## Governance

Worker Agent enforces governance at every step:

- **Sanity Shield**: AI-generated guardrails prevent hallucinated facts
- **Copyright checks**: Scans for potential IP violations
- **Approval gates**: Human review required before publish
- **Audit trail**: Every action is logged with immutable timestamps
- **Brand safety**: Ensures content aligns with brand guidelines

---

## Environment Configuration

See `.env.example` for all available environment variables. Key variables:

| Variable         | Required | Description                     |
|-----------------|----------|---------------------------------|
| DATABASE_URL    | Yes      | PostgreSQL connection string    |
| REDIS_URL       | Yes      | Redis connection string         |
| BETTER_AUTH_SECRET | Yes   | Session signing secret          |
| OPENAI_API_KEY  | Optional | OpenAI API key                  |
| ANTHROPIC_API_KEY | Optional | Anthropic API key             |
| GOOGLE_API_KEY  | Optional | Google API key                  |
| GITHUB_CLIENT_ID | Optional | GitHub OAuth client ID        |
| GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET | Optional | GitHub OAuth secret       |

---

## Deployment

Production deployment uses Docker containers orchestrated via systemd. See the `deployment/` directory for:

- `rc1/001_worker_agent_baseline.sql` — Database schema baseline
- `rc1/verify-schema.sql` — Schema verification script
- `rc1/env.template` — Environment template for production
- `nginx/worker-agent.conf` — Nginx reverse proxy configuration
- `systemd/worker-agent-api.service` — API server systemd unit
- `systemd/worker-agent-worker.service` — Background worker systemd unit
- `scripts/bootstrap.sh` — Server bootstrap script

### Quick Start (Production)

```bash
# 1. Clone and build
git clone https://github.com/CodesbyFebin/Worker-Agent
cd Worker-Agent
npm ci
npm run build

# 2. Configure environment
cp deployment/rc1/env.template .env.production
# Edit .env.production with your values

# 3. Bootstrap server
sudo bash deployment/scripts/bootstrap.sh

# 4. Start services
sudo systemctl start worker-agent-api
sudo systemctl start worker-agent-worker
```

## Development

```bash
# Install dependencies
npm ci

# Start dev servers (API + Web concurrently)
npm run dev

# Type checking
npm run typecheck

# Linting
npm run lint

# Tests
npm run test

# Build for production
npm run build

# Validate everything
npm run validate
```
